   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">ANTERIS TECHNOLOGIES GLOBAL CORP.</span>

   <a id="NOTES" title="NOTES"></a><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">NOTES TO THE CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</span>

  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">FOR THE THREE MONTHS ENDED MARCH 31, 2026</span>
  </div><div>
  </div><div style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div><div>
  </div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" escape="true" name="us-gaap:NatureOfOperations" id="ixv-3434"><div style="text-indent: -28.35pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 28.35pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 28.35pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">1.</span>
    </div>
    <div>
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">DESCRIPTION OF BUSINESS</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 28.35pt; font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">The principal activities of Anteris Technologies Global Corp. (&#8220;ATGC,&#8221; &#8220;Anteris,&#8221; &#8220;Company,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us,&#8221; or &#8220;our&#8221;) include:</span>
  </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div style="text-indent: -27pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 27pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 27.0pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     <span style=" font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">&#9679;</span>
    </div>
    <div>
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">Continued research and development (&#8220;R&amp;D&#8221;) of the DurAVR</span><sup style="font-size: 7.0pt; color: #000000;">&#174;</sup><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">&#160;Transcatheter Heart Valve (&#8220;THV&#8221;), consisting of a single-piece biomimetic valve made with our primary ADAPT</span><sup style="font-size: 7.0pt; color: #000000;">&#174;</sup><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;"> tissue-enhancing technology and deployed with our ComASUR</span><sup style="font-size: 7.0pt; color: #000000;">&#174;</sup><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;"> balloon-expandable delivery system (the &#8220;ComASUR</span><sup style="font-size: 7.0pt; color: #000000;">&#174;</sup><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;"> Delivery System&#8221;), designed to address unmet medical needs in the treatment of aortic stenosis. The DurAVR</span><sup style="font-size: 7.0pt; color: #000000;">&#174;</sup><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;"> THV, with its single piece, native-shaped biomimetic design is built to mimic the performance of a healthy aortic valve and to restore normal laminar blood flow. This new class of technology can be used to treat new aortic stenosis patients and to treat aortic stenosis patients where their current bioprosthetic aortic valve is failing (&#8220;valve-in-valve&#8221;).</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 27pt; font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div style="text-indent: -27pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 27pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 27.0pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     <span style=" font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">&#9679;</span>
    </div>
    <div>
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">Advancing the DurAVR</span><sup style="font-size: 7.0pt; color: #000000;">&#174;</sup><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;"> THV clinical program, including ongoing patient recruitment and data collection for the randomized global pivotal study (the &#8220;PARADIGM Trial&#8221;), expansion into additional geographies, and continued site activation and training. Data from the PARADIGM Trial is intended to support a Premarket Approval (&#8220;PMA&#8221;) application in the United States and a parallel CE Mark approval in Europe. These are key milestones on the path to commercialization.</span>
    </div>
  </div></ix:nonNumeric><div>
  </div><div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 27pt; font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div><div>
  </div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_SignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="us-gaap:SignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" id="ixv-3470"><div style="text-indent: -28.35pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 28.35pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 28.35pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">2.</span>
    </div>
    <div>
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">BASIS OF PRESENTATION AND SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 28.35pt; font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div>
  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="ixv-3477"><div style="text-align: justify;"> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">The condensed consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (&#8220;U.S. GAAP&#8221;). These policies have been consistently applied to all the periods presented, unless otherwise stated. The accompanying condensed consolidated financial statements of the Company are unaudited. In the opinion of management, all adjustments necessary for a fair statement of results of operations, cash flows, and financial position have been made. The results of operations for the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025 are not necessarily indicative of results that may be expected for the full year or any other subsequent interim period.</span> </div></ix:nonNumeric>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <ix:continuation continuedAt="_BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_2" id="_BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_1"><div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">Unless noted otherwise, all dollar amounts are in thousands of United States dollars (&#8220;U.S. dollars&#8221; or &#8220;$&#8221;). Some amounts may not reconcile due to rounding.</span>
  </div></ix:continuation>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <ix:continuation continuedAt="_BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_3" id="_BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_2"><div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">The Company is an emerging growth company (&#8220;EGC&#8221;), as defined in Section 2(a) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the &#8220;Securities Act&#8221;), as modified by the Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act of 2012 (the &#8220;JOBS Act&#8221;), which permits the Company to utilize an extended transition period to comply with new or revised accounting standards applicable to public companies.</span>
  </div></ix:continuation>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <ix:continuation continuedAt="_BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_4" id="_BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_3"><div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with U.S. GAAP requires management to make judgments, estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the financial statements and accompanying notes. Management bases its judgments, estimates and assumptions on historical experience and on other various factors, including expectations of future events that management believe to be reasonable under the circumstances. Actual results could differ from those estimates due to risks and uncertainties.</span>
  </div></ix:continuation>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <ix:continuation continuedAt="_BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_5" id="_BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_4"><div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">The accounting policies adopted in the preparation of the condensed consolidated financial statements are consistent with those adopted and disclosed in the Group&#8217;s (defined below) financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025, and therefore these condensed consolidated financial statements do not include all information and footnote disclosures normally included in the annual consolidated financial statements. The financial information included herein should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and related notes for the year ended December 31, 2025 as included in the</span><span style="font-size: 10.0pt;">&#160;</span><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">Company&#8217;s</span><span style="font-size: 10.0pt;">&#160;</span><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;) on February 26, 2026 (the &#8220;Annual Report&#8221;).</span>
  </div></ix:continuation>
  <div style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <ix:continuation id="_BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_5"><div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">There have been no material changes to the Company's significant accounting policies from those described in the consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025, except for the adoption of certain accounting standards impacting disclosures only, as discussed below.</span>
  </div></ix:continuation>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock" id="ixv-3505"><div style="text-indent: -28.35pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 28.35pt;"> <div style="float: left; width: 28.35pt; white-space: nowrap;"> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-weight: bold;">(a)</span> </div> <div> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-weight: bold;">Principles of consolidation</span> </div> </div></ix:nonNumeric>
  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 28.35pt; font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div>
  <ix:continuation continuedAt="_ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_2" id="_ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_1"><div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">The condensed consolidated financial statements include the accounts of ATGC, its wholly-owned subsidiaries, entities for which the Company has a controlling financial interest, as well as any variable interest entities (&#8220;VIEs&#8221;) for which ATGC has been determined to be the primary beneficiary. ATGC and its subsidiaries together are referred to in these financial statements as the &#8220;Group.&#8221;</span>
  </div></ix:continuation>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <ix:continuation id="_ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_2"><div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">Subsidiaries are all those entities over which the Group has control. Control is the power to govern the financial and operating policies of an entity. All subsidiaries of ATGC have a reporting year end of December 31. Intercompany transactions, balances and unrealized gains or losses on transactions between entities in the Group are eliminated.</span>
  </div></ix:continuation>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="ixv-3520"><div style="text-indent: -28.35pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 28.35pt;"> <div style="float: left; width: 28.35pt; white-space: nowrap;"> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-weight: bold;">(b)</span> </div> <div> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-weight: bold;">Recently Adopted Accounting Standards</span> </div> </div></ix:nonNumeric>
  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 28.35pt; font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div>
  <ix:continuation id="_NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_1"><div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">In December 2023, the Financial Accounting Standard Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) 2023-09, </span><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-style: italic;">Income Taxes (Topic 740) Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures</span><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">. ASU 2023-09 intends to enhance income tax disclosures to address investor requests for more information about the tax risks and opportunities present in an entity&#8217;s worldwide operations and primarily requires further disaggregation of existing disclosures related to the effective tax rate reconciliation and income taxes paid. As an EGC, the Company elected to apply the extended transition period, and will adopt ASU 2023&#8209;09 for the year ending December 31, 2026. The ASU impacts disclosure only and did not have an impact on the Company&#8217;s condensed consolidated financial statements. The Company will apply the disclosure requirements prospectively beginning with the year ending December 31, 2026; however, for comparability, the Company expects to present comparative income tax disclosures for the year ended December 31, 2025 in its annual financial statements for the year ending December 31, 2026, as applicable.</span>
  </div></ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric><div>
  </div><div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div><div>

  </div><div style="width: 100%; font-family: TimesNewRoman, &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, Baskerville, Georgia, serif; font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px; text-indent: 0px; font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; text-decoration: none;">

   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">FOR THE THREE MONTHS ENDED MARCH 31, 2026</span>

  </div><div style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div><div>

    <div style="float: left; width: 27.0pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">2.</span>
    </div>
    <div>
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">BASIS OF PRESENTATION AND</span><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">&#160;</span><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (continued)</span>
    </div>
  </div><div>
  </div><div style="margin-left: 27pt; font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div><div>
  </div><ix:continuation id="_SignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock-c0_cont_1"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="avr_NewAccountingStandardsNotYetAdoptedPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="avr:NewAccountingStandardsNotYetAdoptedPolicyTextBlock" id="ixv-3568"><div style="text-indent: -28.35pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 28.35pt;"> <div style="float: left; width: 28.35pt; white-space: nowrap;"> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-weight: bold;">(c)</span> </div> <div> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-weight: bold;">New Accounting Standards Not Yet Adopted</span> </div> </div></ix:nonNumeric>
  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 28.35pt; font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div>
  <ix:continuation continuedAt="avr_NewAccountingStandardsNotYetAdoptedPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_2" id="avr_NewAccountingStandardsNotYetAdoptedPolicyTextBlock-c0_cont_1"><div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">The FASB has not issued any accounting standards updates during the first three months of 2026.</span>
  </div></ix:continuation>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;

   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">For information on accounting pronouncements issued in prior years but not yet adopted, refer to Note 2(y) in the consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025</span><span style="font-size: 10.0pt;">&#160;</span><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">as included in the Annual Report.</span>

  </div><div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div><div>
  </div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" escape="true" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxDisclosureTextBlock" id="ixv-3587"><div style="text-indent: -28.35pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 28.35pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 28.35pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">3.</span>
    </div>
    <div>
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">INCOME TAX</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 28.35pt; font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify;"> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">The Company&#8217;s provision for interim periods is determined using an estimate of the annual effective tax rate, adjusted for discrete items arising in that period. The Company&#8217;s effective tax rate differs from the U.S. statutory tax rate primarily due to valuation allowances on its deferred tax assets as it is more likely than not that some, or all, of the Company&#8217;s deferred tax assets will not be realized. Income tax expense for the three months ended March 31, 2026 includes a discrete tax expense related to a Swiss withholding tax settlement arising from a prior&#8209;period tax audit. There was <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c2" decimals="-3" format="ixt:fixed-zero" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="3" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-6529">no</ix:nonFraction> income tax benefit for the three months ended March 31, 2025.</span> </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">Deferred tax assets and liabilities are determined based upon the differences between the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements carrying amounts and the tax bases of existing assets and liabilities and for loss and credit carryforwards, using enacted tax rates expected to be in effect in the years in which the differences are expected to reverse. The Company has provided a full valuation allowance against the net deferred tax assets as the Company has determined that it was more likely than not that the Company would not realize the benefits of net deferred tax assets.</span>
  </div></ix:nonNumeric><div>
  </div><div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div><div>
  </div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" escape="true" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsDisclosureTextBlock" id="ixv-3602"><div style="text-indent: -28.35pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 28.35pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 28.35pt; white-space: nowrap;">

    <div style="float: left; width: 28.35pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">9.</span>
    </div>
    <div>
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">VARIABLE INTEREST ENTITY</span></div>
  <div>&#160;</div></div>









  <div><span style="letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important;">The Company has agreed to provide certain development services to v2vmedtech, inc. (&#8220;v2vmedtech&#8221;) in exchange for equity in v2vmedtech. The Company provides engineering, clinical, regulatory, marketing, and executive management resources, but excluding medical and chief medical officer services, in connection with v2vmedtech&#8217;s development of an innovative heart valve repair device utilizing a transcatheter edge-to-edge repair method for a minimally invasive treatment of mitral and tricuspid valve regurgitation, also known as leaky valve.</span></div><div>&#160;</div><div><span style="letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important;">he Company has determined that v2vmedtech is a VIE under ASC 810 and that the Company is the primary beneficiary because it has the power to direct the activities that most significantly affect v2vmedtech&#8217;s economic performance, primarily through appointing and holding a majority of the v2vmedtech&#8217;s board of directors, and has the right to receive certain benefits or the obligation to absorb losses that could potentially be significant to v2vmedtech through equity ownership. Therefore, the Company consolidates v2vmedtech and reassesses its primary&#8209;beneficiary status at each reporting date.</span></div><div>&#160;</div><div><span style="letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">Subsequent to March 31, 2026,&#160;the Company terminated the Contribution and Stock Purchase Agreement with v2vmedtech, as described in Note 12&#160;</span><span style="letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; font-style: italic;">Subsequent Events</span><span style="letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">, after which the Company no longer has ongoing development funding obligations.</span></div></ix:nonNumeric><div>&#160;</div><div>


  </div><div style="width: 100%; font-family: TimesNewRoman, &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, Baskerville, Georgia, serif; font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px; text-indent: 0px; font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; text-decoration: none;">

This loan has been provided to support v2vmedtech&#8217;s working capital needs. It is unsecured and repayable on demand. This balance is eliminated in the condensed consolidated financial statements. Other than the initial capital contributions of other stockholders of v2vmedtech, v2vmedtech is wholly financed by the Group. In exchange for v2vmedtech equity interests, the Group contributed $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c81" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:VariableInterestEntityFinancialOrOtherSupportAmount" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-6648">0.2</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c82" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:VariableInterestEntityFinancialOrOtherSupportAmount" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-6649">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million to v2vmedtech to finance its operations during the three months ended March 31, 2026 and March 31, 2025, respectively.</span></div></ix:continuation><div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" escape="true" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock" id="ixv-4568"><div style="text-indent: -28.35pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 28.35pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 28.35pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">10.</span>
    </div>
    <div>
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 28.35pt; font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-style: italic;">Commitments</span>
  </div>

  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</div><div style="text-align: justify;"> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">As of each of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, the Group had capital commitments of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:LongTermPurchaseCommitmentAmount" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-6650"><ix:nonFraction contextRef="c83" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:LongTermPurchaseCommitmentAmount" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-6651">0.1</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> million for the purchase of plant and equipment.</span> </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div>
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-style: italic;">Contingencies</span>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div>
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">The Group records a liability in the consolidated financial statements on an undiscounted basis for loss contingencies related to legal actions when a loss is considered probable, and the amount may be reasonably estimated. If the reasonable estimate of a probable loss is a range, and no amount within the range is a better estimate than any other, the minimum amount of the range is accrued. If a loss is reasonably possible but not probable, and may be reasonably estimated, the estimated loss or range of loss is disclosed. When determining the estimated loss or range of loss, significant judgment is required. Estimates of probable losses resulting from litigation and governmental proceedings involving the Company are inherently difficult to predict, particularly when the matters are in early procedural stages with incomplete scientific facts or legal discovery, involve unsubstantiated or indeterminate claims for damages, potentially involve penalties, fines or punitive damages, or could result in a change in business practice.</span>
  </div></ix:nonNumeric><div>
  </div><div style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div><div>
  </div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock" id="ixv-4589"><div style="text-indent: -28.35pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 28.35pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 28.35pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">11.</span>
    </div>
    <div>
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">SEGMENT REPORTING</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 28.35pt; font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div>
    <div style="float: left; width: 36.0pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">(a)</span>
    </div>
    <div>
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">Description of segments</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify;"> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">Segment information is presented using a management approach, meaning that segment information is provided on the same basis as information is used for internal reporting purposes by the chief operating decision maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;) which is the Company&#8217;s Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, who makes key strategic decisions. The CODM is responsible for the allocation of resources and assessing the performance of the Group. Management has determined that the activities of the business as reviewed by the CODM are <ix:nonFraction contextRef="c0" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" scale="0" unitRef="Segment" id="ixv-6652">one</ix:nonFraction> segment, being the development and commercialization of the ADAPT</span><sup style="font-size: 7.0pt; color: #000000;">&#174;</sup><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;"> anti-calcification tissue. This is focused on the DurAVR</span><sup style="font-size: 7.0pt; color: #000000;">&#174;</sup><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;"> THV System.</span> </div>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div>
    <div style="float: left; width: 36.0pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">(b)</span>
    </div>
    <div>
     <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">Segment information</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size: 10pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div>
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">The revenue and cost information relating to all of the ADAPT</span><sup style="font-size: 7.0pt; color: #000000;">&#174;</sup><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;"> products including both the DurAVR</span><sup style="font-size: 7.0pt; color: #000000;">&#174;</sup><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;"> THV System and regenerative tissue products are regularly reviewed by the CODM on an aggregate basis.</span>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000;">The CODM assesses performance and allocates resources based on the Company&#8217;s Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations and key components and processes of the Company&#8217;s operations are managed centrally. Segment asset information is not used by the CODM to allocate resources. <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c0" continuedAt="_ScheduleOfSegmentReportingInformationBySegmentTextBlock-c0_cont_1" escape="true" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfSegmentReportingInformationBySegmentTextBlock" id="ixv-6653">As a single reportable segment entity, the Company&#8217;s segment performance measure is net income or loss.</ix:nonNumeric></span><span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">&#160;</span></div></ix:nonNumeric><div>

  </div><div>&#160;</div><div>




  </div><div style="width: 100%; font-family: TimesNewRoman, &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, Baskerville, Georgia, serif; font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px; text-indent: 0px; font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; text-decoration: none;">

  </div><div>
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">NOTES TO THE CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</span>
  </div><div>

   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">Brooklyn Park Lease</span>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt;">On April 23, 2026, the Company, through a wholly owned subsidiary, entered into a lease agreement for office and warehouse space located in Brooklyn Park, Minnesota. The lease term commences on September 1, 2026. In connection with the lease, the Company entered into an irrevocable standby letter of credit in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c98" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="us-gaap:LettersOfCreditOutstandingAmount" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-6680">3.5</ix:nonFraction> million, in favor of the landlord to secure certain obligations under the lease. The standby letter of credit expires on <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c99" format="ixt:date-monthname-day-year-en" name="avr:LettersOfCreditExpirationDate" id="ixv-6681">April 21, 2027</ix:nonNumeric>, subject to automatic annual renewal unless notice of non&#8209;extension is provided by the issuing bank.</span> </div>
  <div style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div>
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt;">The lease represents a non recognized subsequent event, and no lease assets or liabilities have been recorded in the condensed consolidated financial statements as the lease commencement date occurs after March 31, 2026. The Company will evaluate and recognize the lease in accordance with ASC 842 upon commencement of the lease term.</span>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;

  <div>
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">Termination of v2v Agreement</span>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div> <span style="font-size: 10.0pt;">On April 28, 2026, the Company, through a wholly owned subsidiary, notified v2vmedtech that it had elected to discontinue further development contributions under the Contribution and Stock Purchase Agreement dated April 18, 2023. As a result of this election, the Company is required to pay a contractual break fee of $<ix:nonFraction contextRef="c100" decimals="-5" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" name="avr:ContractualBreakFeePayable" scale="6" unitRef="usd" id="ixv-6682">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million and has no further obligation to fund development activities. Following payment of the break fee, the related development agreement will terminate.</span> </div>
  <div style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;
  </div>
  <div>
   <span style="font-size: 10.0pt;">Under the terms of the agreement, the initial shareholders of v2vmedtech may elect to either acquire the Company&#8217;s equity interest or reduce it to a capped minority interest. The Company does not expect this matter to have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position or liquidity.</span>

  </div><div style="text-indent: -36pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 36pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 36.0pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     <span style="font-weight: bold;">Item 2.</span>
    </div>
    <div style="text-indent: -36px; padding-left: 36px;">
     <a id="Managements" title="Management&#8217;s"></a><span style="font-weight: bold;">Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</span>
    </div>
  </div><div style="text-align: justify; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   <span style="font-style: italic;">The following Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (&#8220;MD&amp;A&#8221;) should be read in conjunction with our condensed consolidated financial statements and related notes appearing elsewhere in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q and our annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;) on February 26, 2026 (the &#8220;Annual Report&#8221;). Except for historical information, the matters discussed in this MD&amp;A contain various forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties and are based upon judgments concerning various factors beyond our control. Our actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements. Please also see the section of this Form 10-Q titled &#8220;Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements.&#8221;</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-weight: bold;">Overview</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   <span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">Anteris is a structural heart company dedicated to revolutionizing cardiac care by pioneering science-driven and measurable advancements to restore heart valve patients to healthy function. Our lead product, the DurAVR</span><sup style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">&#174;</sup><span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">&#160;Transcatheter Heart Valve (&#8220;THV&#8221;) System, was designed in collaboration with the world&#8217;s leading interventional cardiologists and cardiac surgeons to treat aortic stenosis &#8212; a potentially life-threatening condition resulting from a narrowing of the aortic valve. The balloon-expandable DurAVR</span><sup style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">&#174;</sup><span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);"> THV is the first biomimetic valve, which is shaped to mimic the performance of a healthy human aortic valve and aims to replicate normal aortic blood flow. Our DurAVR</span><sup style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">&#174;</sup><span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);"> THV System consists of a single-piece, biomimetic valve made with our proprietary ADAPT</span><sup style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">&#174;</sup><span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);"> tissue-enhancing technology and deployed with our </span>ComASUR<sup>&#174;</sup> balloon-expandable delivery system (the &#8220;ComASUR<sup>&#174;</sup> Delivery System&#8221;)<span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">. ADAPT</span><sup style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">&#174;</sup><span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);"> is our proprietary anti-calcification tissue shaping technology that is designed to reengineer xenograft tissue into a pure, single-piece collagen bioscaffold. Our patented ADAPT</span><sup style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">&#174;</sup><span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);"> tissue has been clinically demonstrated to be calcium free for up to 10 years post-procedure, according to </span><span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32); font-style: italic;">Performance of the ADAPT-Treated CardioCel</span><sup style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32); font-style: italic;">&#174;</sup><span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32); font-style: italic;"> Scaffold in Pediatric Patients With Congenital Cardiac Anomalies: Medium to Long-Term Outcomes</span><span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">, published by William Neethling et al., and has been distributed for use in over 55,000 patients globally in other indications. Our ComASUR</span><sup style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">&#174;</sup><span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);"> Delivery System, which was developed in consultation with physicians, is designed to provide precise alignment with the heart&#8217;s native commissures to achieve accurate placement of the DurAVR</span><sup style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">&#174;</sup><span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);"> THV.</span>
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   <span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">We intend to establish the safety and effectiveness of the DurAVR</span><sup style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);">&#174;</sup><span style="color: rgb(35, 31, 32);"> THV in patients with severe aortic stenosis in our global pivotal study (the &#8220;PARADIGM Trial&#8221;).</span>
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   &#160;The PARADIGM Trial is a prospective, randomized, controlled multicenter, international study wherein subjects will be randomized to receive either a transcatheter aortic valve replacement (&#8220;TAVR&#8221;) using the DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup> THV or TAVR using a commercially available and approved THV in an &#8220;All Comers Randomized Cohort.&#8221; The primary end point of the PARADIGM Trial is a composite of all-cause mortality, all stroke and cardiovascular hospitalization at one year post-procedure. The endpoint will be evaluated as a non-inferiority analysis. Subjects with a failed surgical bioprosthesis in need of a valve-in-valve TAVR will be enrolled in a separate parallel registry.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div style="margin: 0in; text-indent: 0.5in; font-size: 10pt;">Recruitment to the PARADIGM Trial commenced
in Europe in October 2025, followed by receipt of FDA Investigational Device
Exemption (&#8220;IDE&#8221;) approval for the trial in November 2025. In April 2026, we
secured U.S. Medicare reimbursement eligibility for the global pivotal PARADIGM
Trial under a Centers for Medicare &amp; Medicaid Services (&#8220;CMS&#8221;) national
coverage policy. Eligible procedures performed at participating U.S. study
sites are covered under the Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) National
Coverage Determination 20.32. This milestone supported the activation of our
initial U.S. sites as part of the PARADIGM Trial with
first patients enrolled and treated during May 2026.</div><div style="margin: 0in; font-size: 12pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</span></div><div style="margin: 0in; font-size: 12pt; text-indent: 0.5in;"><span style="font-size: 10pt;">Recruitment remains ongoing, with planned
expansion into additional countries to further accelerate patient enrollment.
The PARADIGM Trial is supported by early clinical experience from over 130
patients treated with the DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup> THV.</span></div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">

  &#160;</div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   It is anticipated that the design of the PARADIGM Trial will provide the primary clinical evidence on which the FDA could base a decision for Premarket Approval (&#8220;PMA&#8221;), which is required for commercialization of the DurAVR<sup>&#174; </sup>THV System in the United States. We anticipate CE Mark approval will progress in parallel to the PMA.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-weight: bold;">Financial Overview</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   As a development-stage company, we have incurred losses since our inception. We anticipate that we will continue to incur losses for the foreseeable future and there can be no assurance that we will ever achieve or maintain profitability.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   We expect expenses for our research, clinical validation, development, design, manufacturing and marketing will increase and, as a result, we will need additional capital to fund our operations. Any future funding could involve a combination of equity offerings, debt financings, other third-party funding, marketing and distribution arrangements, strategic alliances and licensing arrangements. We may be unable to raise additional funds or enter into such other arrangements when needed on favorable terms or at all.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   In January 2026, we completed an underwritten public offering, pursuant to which we issued and sold 40,000,000 shares of our Common Stock, including the full exercise of the underwriters&#8217; option to purchase additional shares, at a public offering price of $5.75 per share (the &#8220;2026 Public Offering&#8221;) and a stock purchase agreement with Covidien Group S.&#224; r.l. (&#8220;Medtronic&#8221;), a wholly owned subsidiary of Medtronic plc, pursuant to which we issued and sold to Medtronic 15,652,173 shares of Common Stock at a purchase price of $5.75 per share (the &#8220;Medtronic Private Placement&#8221;), which collectively generated gross proceeds of approximately $320.0 million, before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions, placement agent fees, and offering expenses.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Any failure to raise capital or enter into such other arrangements as and when needed could have a negative impact on our financial condition and our ability to market our products.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="width: 100%; font-family: TimesNewRoman, &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, Baskerville, Georgia, serif; font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px; text-indent: 0px; font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; text-decoration: none;">
  <div style="text-align: center">12</div>
  <div style="break-after: page;"><hr style="border-width: medium; border-style: none; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: initial; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: black; background-color: black;"/></div>
<div class="header override"><div style="text-align: left; font-size: 8pt; font-style: italic;"><a href="#TO">Table of Contents</a></div></div></div><div>
   <span style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Principles of Consolidation and Operating Segments</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   The condensed consolidated financial statements include the accounts for our company, our wholly-owned subsidiaries, and entities for which we have a controlling financial interest. Intercompany transactions, balances and unrealized gains and losses on transactions between such entities are eliminated.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Our management has determined that the activities of the business as reviewed by our Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, who also serves as our chief operating decision maker, are one segment, being the development and commercialization of the ADAPT<sup>&#174;</sup> anti-calcification tissue. This is focused on the DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup> THV System.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Components of Results of Operations</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">Revenue and Other Income</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   We currently derive revenue from the sale of regenerative tissue products. Such sales have historically been made principally to 4C Medical Technologies, Inc. (&#8220;4C&#8221;) and, in prior periods, to LeMaitre Vascular, Inc. (&#8220;LeMaitre&#8221;), a distributor of medical products. In 2019, we sold the distribution rights for CardioCel&#8482; and VascuCel&#8482; to LeMaitre in order to focus on development of our proprietary ADAPT<sup>&#174;</sup> tissue for the DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup> THV System and, in connection therewith, we entered into a Transition Services Agreement pursuant to which we manufactured and sold CardioCel&#8482; and VascuCel&#8482; products to LeMaitre. The Transition Services Agreement with LeMaitre expired in January 2025, and we do not expect to receive any future revenue from LeMaitre.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   The Supply and License Agreement with 4C (the &#8220;4C Agreement&#8221;), had an initial seven-year term that ended on June 1, 2025, and under its terms would automatically renew for successive one-year periods unless either party provided written notice of non-renewal at least 180 days prior to the applicable renewal date. On November 26, 2025, we notified 4C that we would not renew the 4C Agreement for the next renewal term. The agreement will expire on June 1, 2026, and no early termination penalties are anticipated in connection with its non-renewal. The expiration of the 4C Agreement is not expected to have a material impact on our financial results.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">Expenses</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Our most significant expenses are research and development (&#8220;R&amp;D&#8221;) and selling, general and administrative expenses.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Cost of products sold in 2026 reflects the manufacturing cost from the sale of regenerative tissue products to 4C. In 2025, cost of products sold also included manufacturing costs related to sales to LeMaitre. These expenditures include raw materials and consumables, plus other costs attributable to the manufacturing of these products.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">R&amp;D Expense</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   R&amp;D has been a significant focus with investments in the DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup> THV System, including the DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup> THV, the ComASUR<sup>&#174;</sup>&#160;Delivery System, a disposable crimper, and an expandable access sheath. These components are collectively managed as part of the overall DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup> THV System rather than as separate projects. Since late 2021, when our DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup> THV was first used in human trials in Tbilisi, Georgia, R&amp;D efforts have focused on incorporating clinical insights to refine and advance the technology, supporting the pathway toward commercialization. These costs have included, among others, preclinical and clinical studies, design iterations, lab services, clinical data monitoring, project and site management, travel, data management and safety of the study.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   During the three months ended March 31, 2026, the Anteris team continued to expand global manufacturing capacity to scale for the PARADIGM Trial. All production (DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup> THV, ComASUR<sup>&#174;</sup> Delivery System, crimper, E-sheath) is being scaled into new ISO Qualified Clean Room facilities, increasing manufacturing capacity relative to 2025 capacity levels. The transition to the new facilities aims for a reliable and scaled inventory supply to support the PARADIGM Trial. In addition, the gold-standard ADAPT<sup>&#174;</sup> tissue for the DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup> THV is planned to be sourced from both the United States and Australia moving forward to help mitigate supply chain risks. This progress reflects the strategic deployment of capital into areas that support operational readiness and long-term growth capacity for clinical and commercial success.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>

  </div><div style="width: 100%; font-family: TimesNewRoman, &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, Baskerville, Georgia, serif; font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px; text-indent: 0px; font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; text-decoration: none;">
  <div style="text-align: center;">13</div>
  <div style="break-after: page;"><hr style="border-width: medium; border-style: none; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: initial; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: black; background-color: black;"/></div>
<div class="header override"><div style="text-align: left; font-size: 8pt; font-style: italic;"><a href="#TO">Table of Contents</a></div></div></div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">Net Sales</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Net sales during the three months ended March 31, 2026 was $0.5 million, compared to $0.6 million for the same period in the prior year. The decrease of $0.1 million was primarily due to net sales in the three months ended March 31, 2025 included $0.3 million from the sale of CardioCel&#8482; and VascuCel&#8482; products to LeMaitre in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, which expired in January 2025, offset by an increase of net sales of tissue products to 4C increasing by $0.2 million in the three months ended March 31, 2026 compared to the prior year.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">Cost of Products Sold</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Cost of products sold during the three months ended March 31, 2026 was $0.1 million, a decrease of $0.1 million (45%), compared to $0.2 million for the same period in the prior year. The decrease in cost of products sold was primarily due to the inclusion in the three months ended March 31, 2025 of amounts associated with sales of CardioCel&#8482; and VascuCel&#8482; products under the Transition Services Agreement with LeMaitre. This decrease was partially offset by increased production volumes due to increases in demand for tissue products from 4C in 2026.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">R&amp;D Expense</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   R&amp;D expenses during the three months ended March 31, 2026 were $17.5 million, an increase of $1.0 million (6%), compared to $16.5 million for the same period in the prior year. This increase was primarily due to an increase of $2.0 million in the three months ended March 31, 2026 related to the upscaling of manufacturing and quality capabilities, including process design and validation activities and the expansion of headcount, and an increase of $1.0 million related to activities linked to the PARADIGM Trial, including the scaling of our field based clinical team. These were partly offset by reduced DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup>&#160;product research costs of $2.0 million as we shifted our focus to clinical, regulatory and manufacturing activities ahead of the PARADIGM Trial.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">Selling, General and Administrative Expense</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt;">
   Selling, general and administrative expenses during the three months ended March 31, 2026 were $6.9 million, an increase of $1.3 million (22%) compared to the same period in the prior year, which increase was primarily due to higher employee related costs, increased share based payment expenses, and additional consulting costs.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">Other non-operating income, net</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Other non-operating income, net&#160;during the three months ended March 31, 2026 was $1.7 million, an increase of $1.6 million compared to $0.1 million for the same period in the prior year, which increase was primarily due to interest earned on money-market fund deposits following the January 2026 capital raises.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">Net Foreign Exchange (Losses)/Gains</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Net foreign exchange losses during the three months ended March 31, 2026 were $0.1 million compared to $0.2 million of net foreign exchange losses for the same period in the prior year, which amounted to a decrease of $0.1 million (57%), primarily due to the change in foreign exchange rates on intercompany and cash balances. In the first quarter of 2026, the United States dollar depreciated by 2% relative to the Australian dollar (&#8220;AUD $&#8221;). In the first quarter of 2025, the United States dollar depreciated by 1% relative to the AUD $.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">Income tax (expense)/benefit</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Income tax expense during the three months ended March 31, 2026 was $0.5 million, compared to nil for the same period in the prior year, representing an increase of $0.5 million, primarily due to the recognition of withholding tax expense incurred during the period in connection with amounts payable by the Company&#8217;s Swiss subsidiary.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-weight: bold;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Capital Requirements and Sources of Liquidity</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   We have experienced recurring operating losses and cash outflows from operating activities since inception. As of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $393.6 million and $370.5 million, respectively.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   In recent years, our operations have primarily been financed through the issuance of capital stock as well as through convertible notes, sales of regenerative tissue products and R&amp;D tax incentives from the Australian government. We have also generated additional funding through interest earned on cash deposits. As of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of $283.2 million and $12.6 million, respectively. As of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, we had capital commitments of $3.0 million and $2.2&#160;<span style="letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 48px; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important;">million, respectively</span> relating to the lease of properties, and we did not have any other material capital expenditure commitments or contingent liabilities.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   We anticipate that we will require additional funds in order to achieve our long-term goals including completing the R&amp;D of our current products. We do not expect to generate significant revenue until we obtain regulatory approval to market and sell our products and sales of our products have commenced. We therefore expect to continue to incur substantial losses in the near future. However, based on our current operating plan, we believe that our existing cash and cash equivalents will be sufficient to meet our operating requirements for at least the next 12 months.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div style="width: 100%; font-family: TimesNewRoman, &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, Baskerville, Georgia, serif; font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px; text-indent: 0px; font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; text-decoration: none;">
  <div style="text-align: center;">14</div>
  <div style="break-after: page;"><hr style="border-width: medium; border-style: none; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: initial; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: black; background-color: black;"/></div>
<div class="header override"><div style="text-align: left; font-size: 8pt; font-style: italic;"><a href="#TO">Table of Contents</a></div></div></div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Our future capital requirements are difficult to forecast and will depend on many factors, including:
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: -27pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 47.25pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 27pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     &#8226;
    </div>
    <div>
     the scope, results and timing of clinical trials&#894;
    </div>
  </div><div style="margin-left: 2.4pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: -27pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 47.25pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 27pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     &#8226;
    </div>
    <div>
     the costs of preparing and completing the PARADIGM Trial of our DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup> THV System&#894;
    </div>
  </div><div style="margin-left: 2.4pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: -27pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 47.25pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 27pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     &#8226;
    </div>
    <div>
     the costs and time required to obtain PMA from the FDA for our DurAVR<sup>&#174;</sup> THV System&#894; and
    </div>
  </div><div style="margin-left: 2.4pt; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: -27pt; text-align: justify; padding-left: 47.25pt;">
    <div style="float: left; width: 27pt; white-space: nowrap;">
     &#8226;
    </div>
    <div>
     the costs of establishing marketing, sales and distribution capabilities.
    </div>
  </div><div style="clear: both;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   We may seek to raise any necessary capital through a combination of public or private equity offerings or debt financings. If we raise additional capital through debt financing, we may be subject to covenants limiting or restricting our ability to take specific actions, such as incurring additional debt, making capital expenditures or declaring dividends. If we decide to raise capital by issuing equity securities, the issuance of such equity securities may result in dilution to our existing stockholders. We cannot give any assurance that we will be successful in completing any financings or that any such equity or debt financing will be available to us if and when required or on satisfactory terms.

  </table><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">Operating Activities</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Net cash used in operating activities during the three months ended March 31, 2026 was $28.7 million, an increase of $7.2 million (33%), compared to $21.5 million in the same period in the prior year, primarily due to higher cash expenditures for R&amp;D, including costs relating to the upscaling of manufacturing capabilities including process design and validation activities, preparatory and ongoing activities linked to the PARADIGM Trial, an increase in salaries and wages from a growth in headcount and the timing of payments to suppliers, including the settlement of liabilities outstanding at December 31, 2025.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">Investing Activities</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Net cash used in investing activities during the three months ended March 31, 2026 was $0.2 million, compared to net cash provided of $1.1 million in the same period in the prior year, a decrease of $1.3 million (116%). This decrease was primarily due to the receipt of $1.4 million of deferred proceeds from LeMaitre in the prior year, relating to the 2019 sale of distribution rights, for which there was no corresponding inflow in the current year. Additionally, cash outflows for purchases of plant and equipment during the three months ended March 31, 2026 were $0.1 million lower than in the same period in 2025.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">Financing Activities</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Net cash provided by financing activities during the three months ended March 31, 2026 was $299.5 million, compared to net cash used in financing activities of $1.1 million in the same period of the prior year, reflecting an increase of $300.6 million. During the three months ended March 31, 2026, we received proceeds of $308.3 million from the issuance of shares of Common Stock net of underwriting fees, which were partially offset by $8.2 million of share issuance transaction costs. In the three months ended March 31, 2025, proceeds of $0.6 million were received related to share issues and cash outflows of $1.2 million were incurred related to transaction costs from the 2024 public offering. Additionally, we repaid $0.6 million of outstanding insurance-related supplier financing debt during the period, representing an increase of $0.1 million compared to the same period in the prior year.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-weight: bold;">Contractual Obligations and Commitments</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-style: italic;">Leases</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   We lease laboratory and manufacturing facilities and offices. The leases typically include options to renew at which time the lease payments are subject to market adjustments and/or set price increases. Extension and termination options are included in a number of the leases to allow for flexibility in terms of corporate growth and managing the assets used in our operations. The leases expire between April 2026 and April 2030 and some include options to extend. At March 31, 2026, we had contractual commitments (on an undiscounted basis) for property leases of $3.5 million, which were recognized on a discounted basis at $3.0 million.

   <span style="font-weight: bold;">Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   We have used various accounting policies to prepare the condensed consolidated financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (&#8220;U.S. GAAP&#8221;).
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   The preparation of condensed consolidated financial statements in conformity with U.S. GAAP requires management to make judgments, estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts in the condensed consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes thereto. Management continually evaluates its judgments and estimates in relation to assets, liabilities, contingent liabilities, revenue and expenses. Management bases its judgments, estimates and assumptions on historical experience and on other various factors, including expectations regarding future events that management believes to be reasonable under the circumstances. Actual results could differ from those estimates due to risks and uncertainties and may be material.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   Our significant accounting policies are discussed in Note 2, &#8220;Basis of Preparation and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&#8221; in our Annual Report. There were no significant changes to these policies during the three months ended March 31, 2026.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify;">&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-weight: bold;">Consolidation of VIEs</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   We consolidate a VIE when the reporting entity (a) has an economic interest in another legal entity (known as a &#8220;variable interest&#8221;) that conveys more than insignificant exposure to potential losses of or benefits from the other legal entity&#894; and (b) has power over the most significant economic activities of the legal entity. There is significant judgment over the analysis to determine whether an entity is a VIE, to determine whether we have a variable interest and to determine whether we are the primary beneficiary of a VIE.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   We determined that v2vmedtech, inc. (&#8220;v2vmedtech&#8221;) is a VIE and that we are the primary beneficiary of v2vmedtech. This determination is based on our having both power over the most significant activities of v2v, primarily through holding a majority of the positions on v2vmedtech&#8217;s board of directors (although v2vmedtech&#8217;s non-Anteris shareholder representative on the v2vmedtech board of directors presently maintains certain veto rights), controlling the appointment of the chief executive officer and chief financial officer roles, being the exclusive partner to develop v2vmedtech&#8217;s products, and benefits through equity ownership.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-weight: bold;">New Accounting Standards Not Yet Adopted</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt;">
   See Note 2 to our condensed financial statements included in Item 1 of this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for more information.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-weight: bold;">Emerging Growth Company and Smaller Reporting Company Status</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   We are an &#8220;emerging growth company&#8221; (an &#8220;EGC&#8221;), as defined in the Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act of 2012 (the &#8220;JOBS Act&#8221;). The JOBS Act provides that an EGC can take advantage of an extended transition period for complying with new or revised accounting standards. This provision allows an EGC to delay the adoption of certain accounting standards until those standards would otherwise apply to private companies. We have elected to avail ourselves of this extended transition period for any new or revised accounting standards during the period in which we remain an EGC.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   As a result, the information that we provide to our investors may be different than what you might receive from other public reporting companies. However, we may adopt certain new or revised accounting standards early.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   We are also a &#8220;smaller reporting company&#8221; (a &#8220;SRC&#8221;), as defined in the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;). We may continue to be a SRC even after we are no longer an EGC. We may take advantage of certain of the scaled disclosures available to SRCs. As a SRC, we will present only two years of audited annual financial statements, plus any required unaudited interim condensed financial statements, and related management&#8217;s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations.

     <span style="font-weight: bold;">Item 4.</span>
    </div>
    <div style="text-indent: -36px; padding-left: 36px;">
     <a id="Controls" title="Controls"></a><span style="font-weight: bold;">Controls and Procedures</span>
    </div>
  </div><div style="clear: both;">&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   As of March 31, 2026, management, with the participation and supervision of our Chief Executive Officer and our Chief Financial Officer, have evaluated our disclosure controls and procedures as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Exchange Act. Based on that evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and our Chief Financial Officer have concluded that, solely as a result of the material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting described below, as of March 31, 2026, our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective to provide reasonable assurance that information we are required to disclose in reports that we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized, and reported within the time periods specified in SEC rules and forms, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div>
   <span style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 35.8pt; text-align: justify; margin-left: 0.2pt;">
   There are no changes in our internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act) that occurred during the three months ended March 31, 2026, that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 0.1pt;">&#160;
  </div><div style="margin-left: 0.2pt;">
   <span style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">Previously Reported Material Weakness</span>
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 35.6pt; text-align: justify; margin-left: 0.3pt;">
   In connection with the preparation of our financial statements for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, our management and our independent auditors identified material weaknesses in the design and operating effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting, which remained unremediated as of December 31, 2025. The material weaknesses identified by our management and our independent auditors relate to (i) a lack of appropriately designed, implemented and documented procedures and controls, and (ii) deficiencies in the segregation of duties.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 0.2pt;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 35.5pt; text-align: justify; margin-left: 0.4pt;">
   A material weakness is a deficiency, or combination of deficiencies, in internal control over financial reporting, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of the annual or interim financial statements will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis.
  </div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 35.7pt; text-align: justify; margin-left: 0.3pt;">
   Management has initiated and continues to implement a remediation plan to address the material weaknesses described above. During the year ended December 31, 2025 and through the quarter ended March 31, 2026, we implemented changes to our internal control over financial reporting, including enhancements to our control environment, improvements to process-level controls, and formal documentation of policies, processes, risks, and controls. Segregation of duties has been enhanced across the control environment and financial reporting systems through system automation, strengthened month-end controls, and enhanced review procedures. Management has commenced testing and is currently validating the operating effectiveness of these enhanced controls, and remediation actions are progressing as planned.
  </div><div style="margin-left: 0.1pt;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 35.8pt; text-align: justify; margin-left: 0.2pt;">
   While we believe that these efforts will improve our internal control over financial reporting, the design and implementation of our remediation is ongoing and will require validation and testing of the design and operating effectiveness of our internal controls over a sustained period of financial reporting cycles. The actions that we are taking are subject to ongoing senior management review, as well as oversight by the Audit and Risk Committee. We will not be able to conclude whether the steps we are taking will fully remediate the material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting until we have completed our remediation efforts and subsequent evaluation of their effectiveness.
  </div><div style="text-align: justify; margin-left: 0.7pt;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: -36pt; text-align: center;">

     <a id="Item_1A" title="Item 1A"></a><span style="font-weight: bold;">Item 1A.</span>
    </div>
    <div style="text-indent: -75px; padding-left: 75px;">
     <span style="font-weight: bold;">Risk Factors</span>
    </div>
  </div><div style="text-align: justify; clear: both;">&#160;
  </div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">
   We face a number of risks that could materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, cash flow, liquidity, or financial condition. Please refer to the factors discussed in Part I, Item 1A. &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; in the Annual Report. Other than the supplemental risk factor provided below, there have been no material changes or additions to our risk factors discussed in such report that could materially impact our business, results of operations, cash flow, liquidity, or financial condition.</div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="font-style: italic; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 48px; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important;">Although we have received regulatory approvals to begin the PARADIGM Trial, there can be no guarantee that the study will be successful or that we will receive PMA from the FDA as a result.</span></div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</div><div style="text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 48px; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important;">Although we have received approval from the FDA to proceed with the PARADIGM Trial under the IDE, the current approval from the FDA to proceed could be revoked, the study could be unsuccessful, and PMA from the FDA may not be obtained or could be revoked. Even if we obtain PMA for our DurAVR</span><sup style="letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 48px; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">&#174;</sup><span style="letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 48px; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important;">&#160;THV System, the FDA or other regulatory authorities may require expensive or burdensome post-market testing or controls. Any delay in, or failure to receive or maintain, clearance or approval for our DurAVR</span><sup style="letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 48px; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial;">&#174;</sup><span style="letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 48px; text-decoration-thickness: initial; text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; float: none; display: inline !important;">&#160;THV System could prevent us from generating revenue or achieving profitability. Additionally, the FDA and other regulatory authorities have broad enforcement powers. Regulatory enforcement or inquiries, or other increased scrutiny on us, could dissuade some physicians from using our products and adversely affect our reputation and the perceived safety and efficacy of our products.</span></div><div>&#160;
  </div><div style="width: 100%; font-family: TimesNewRoman, &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, Baskerville, Georgia, serif; font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px; text-indent: 0px; font-weight: normal; font-style: normal; text-decoration: none;">
